sampling_model.design: Independent samples are drawn from one target population and from each edge-indexed randomized trial; in trial \(e\), treatment is assigned with probability \(1/2\) to each endpoint of \(e\).
sampling_model.units: Each trial unit contributes \((A,Y,X,W,Z_e)\), and each target unit contributes \((X,W)\); all alphabets are fixed and finite.
sampling_model.treatment: The treatment set is \(V=\{0,\ldots,k\}\), with treatment \(0\) the root and the observed randomized comparisons encoded by a directed multigraph \(G=(V,E)\).
sampling_model.overlap: All observed complete cells are at least \(\eta>0\), and each sampling proportion converges to a positive limit.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Cell frequencies estimate \(A_P\), \(b_P\), and \(R_0\).  On a separated-rank class, the truncated weighted moment equation selects \(g_*=M_P^+\Omega^{1/2}b_P\), the minimum Euclidean-norm solution in bridge coordinates; the exact confidence projection instead evaluates \(A_p,b_p,R_p\) jointly at every candidate table and makes no rank selection.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 2.3 gives null-space invariance for a linear functional over a statistical outcome-bridge solution set; it does not construct full-data treatment-network perturbations.
Proposition 2 assumes that both observed bridge sets are nonempty and identifies the pairwise indirect-comparison target from solutions of the corresponding bridge equations.
The finite-proxy causal effect is identified under a full-rank proxy matrix without identification of the measurement mechanism.
The tree-packing theorem characterizes \(q\) edge-disjoint spanning trees by partition cut inequalities.
The matroid partition theorem gives the classical union-rank min--max formula through disjoint independent sets.
Theorem 1 expresses orthogonally invariant treatment-design criteria through the spectrum of a vertex-weighted graph Laplacian.
A strongly identified linear functional admits root-\(n\) asymptotically normal inference despite a weakly identified conditional-moment nuisance.
Proxy variables yield causal-effect bounds without completeness or point identification of a bridge.
Calibrated projection yields uniformly asymptotically valid confidence intervals for scalar projections of moment-identified parameters.
Causally interpretable meta-analysis transports treatment effects from multiple randomized trials using observed effect modifiers.
Regression-based proximal reconciliation compares two trials under parametric latent effect-modification models.
Conditional Wald critical values are robust to arbitrarily weak identification and non-homoskedastic errors in IV and nonlinear GMM.

body.tldr: A finite randomized treatment multigraph can identify transported root contrasts even when every trial-specific bridge is nonunique and the common proxy kernel has structural zeros.  If each covariate stratum has a nonempty proxy carrier positive for every latent class and the required outcome tangents exist only on that carrier, every bridge-null direction lifts to an explicit two-sided interval of observationally equivalent full-data laws.  Thus the target is identified exactly when \(\ker(A_P)\subseteq\ker(R_0)\).  In the rank-one design submodel the exact generic stratum rank is the graphic-union rank \(r_{q_x}(E)\), not merely its saturation value; simultaneous saturation is obtained by a minimum-weight \(q_{\max}\)-fold contracted-union augmentation, where \(q_{\max}=\max_xq_x\).  Separated-rank Wald inference and exact cell-region projection cover regular and rank-unstable regimes, respectively.

project_justification.gap: Published bridge-fiber criteria characterize invariance of statistical solutions, but they do not prove that every target-relevant null direction is realized by two finite full-data causal laws preserving every trial cell and every shared latent node contrast.  Classical tree packing also reports only saturation unless it is connected to the full graphic-matroid-union rank attainable by common stochastic proxy rows.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a support-feasible causal lift coupled to an exact graph-design rank.  It must tolerate proxy structural zeros, distinguish target identification from full bridge recovery, and coordinate heterogeneous covariate-stratum ranks through one trial menu.
project_justification.fill: The paper constructs an active-carrier signed-cell lift, proves exact causal nullity and local ambiguity dimension, represents the generic stratum rank as \(r_{q_x}(E)\), and turns \(q_{\max}\)-fold matroid contraction into an exact-cardinality minimum-cost augmentation.  It then supplies separated-rank Wald inference and rank-free finite-sample projection.

body.related_work: Proposition 2.3 of \cite{ZhangLiMiaoTchetgen2023} studies null-space invariance of a linear functional over a statistical bridge solution set.  The present result is a causal realizability refinement in a different finite treatment-network model, not a same-class theorem inclusion.  Proposition 2 of \cite{SuRytgaardRavnEriksson2026} assumes both observed bridge sets are nonempty and treats a pairwise indirect comparison through a common comparator; it does not give arbitrary-multigraph attainable rank.  The finite-proxy rank perspective of \cite{MiaoGengTchetgen2018} motivates the proxy ceiling, while \cite{DahabrehRobertsonPetitoHernanSteingrimsson2023} transports through observed rather than latent effect modifiers.  The graph certificates are the classical tree-packing theorem of \cite{NashWilliams1961} and matroid-union formula of \cite{Edmonds1965}; the new step is the exact noncancelling-minor representation on attainable stochastic proxy rows and its causal design interpretation.  \cite{Rosa2018} concerns precision design after rank is available.  \cite{BennettEtAl2023} informs regular inference for an identified functional with a nonunique nuisance, and exact Clopper--Pearson projection is used as a conservative finite-sample complement to \cite{KaidoMolinariStoye2019}.  The NETMOTION consumer is \cite{SotiropoulosEtAl2024}, where the proxy-rank ceiling can bind before graph connectivity.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The constructive causal converse uses finite binary potential outcomes, a public finite latent-support bound, a nonempty common active proxy carrier \(J_x\) in each stratum, and anchor-zero one-way tangent surjectivity only on that carrier.  It permits zeros of \(C_x(w\mid u)\) outside \(J_x\) and structural zeros in the joint potential-outcome kernel.  Empty common carriers and genuinely coupled deficient support faces remain a global secant problem: the fixed-completion tangent space is computable, but disconnected latent representations need not be joined by such tangents.  Exact generic rank and the augmentation certificate concern the rank-one observed-row submodel.  The exact confidence projection may be conservative, nonconvex, or nonshrinking near rank changes.
body.honest_scope: Broad sufficiency requires only that every compatible law have a bridge satisfying \(A_Pg=b_P\) and \(\theta=R_0g\).  Necessity is proved on the active-carrier tangent-rich class; its explicit pair of indistinguishable laws transfers nonidentification upward to any supermodel containing that observed-law fiber.  This is not a claim that the Zhang or Su theorem classes are nested in the present class.  The exact generic design rank is \(r_{q_x}(E)\); the \(q_x\)-tree condition is precisely its saturation corollary, and a single graph simultaneously saturates all strata at the \(q_{\max}\)-tree threshold.  Full bridge recovery additionally requires \(q_x=d=|\mathcal W|\).  The NETMOTION interpretation is conditional on valid harmonized proxies, shared latent node contrasts, and an independent target sample.
body.interpretation: The observable operator separates three distinct questions.  The equality \(A_Pg=b_P\) describes bridge representatives; annihilation \(R_0\ker(A_P)=\{0\}\) identifies the causal target without identifying the bridge; and the graphic-union rank \(r_{q_x}(E)\) measures how much of the proxy-effective bridge space a graph can generically learn.  Proxy categories outside \(J_x\) may have structural zeros and need not be smoothed.  Adding trials can increase the union rank only up to \(q_x(|V|-1)\), so it cannot defeat a low-rank common proxy kernel or recover all \(W\)-indexed bridge coordinates unless \(q_x=d\).
